findings.reason: the q95 band is unmeasurable as written and would be reported as a fit failure on every case, so the section needs either a sign canonicalisation of the reference or a stated |q95| comparison.
findings.text: §2 clause (1) sets "q95 within 2.0" against imas-efit's stored state, but the named reference carries `q_95 = -5.79` on its own slices (read through imas-python at DD 4.1.0 from `imas-efit/tests/data/imas/MASTU/45272/regression/magnetics`: slice 0 `q_95=-5.869`, slice 4 `-5.787`, slice 7 `-5.668`, with `ip=+765 kA`), while nova's convention-clean frame defines the q sign as `sign(q) = sigma_Ip * sigma_B0 * sigma_rho_theta_phi` (`nova/scripts/identify_source_cocos.py:29`), so a convention-clean reconstructed q95 of about +5.8 differs from the reference by roughly 11.6 and misses the band by sign alone

findings.reason: without a stated flux-datum alignment (or a span-only comparison) this band fails or passes for a reason unrelated to the fit, which is the confounding the case set was chosen to avoid.
findings.text: §2 clause (1) compares "boundary and axis flux within 5 % of the axis-to-boundary flux span" across two codes, but poloidal flux carries an arbitrary additive datum: the stored reference has `psi_axis=0.6461`, `psi_boundary=0.1389` at slice 0 and `psi_axis=0.0661`, `psi_boundary=-0.4908` at slice 7, so its boundary flux is not zero and its datum drifts over the pulse, while the clause names no alignment rule, so the band cannot be evaluated

findings.reason: the house convention for a sibling plan is `/nova/plans/<slug>` and the target document does exist at `docs/plans/spine-efit-parity.html`, so this is a one-line href repair that changes no declaration, band or decision.
findings.text: the §0 citation `<a href="/nova/spine-efit-parity">` resolves, under the docs surface's `.html` convention, to `docs/spine-efit-parity.html`, which does not exist, so the evidence for the plan's opening claim ("the assembled chain failed 10 of 12 EFIT parity metrics with no converged fraction on MAST") cannot be reached
